content:
maya: Heads-up — seeing gaps in private VPC telemetry for keystore access after the last RBAC rollout. Some decrypt calls from the keystore-proxy pod aren't producing k8s audit events. Not sure if this is KMS proxy, netpol, or RBAC edge case.
ben: Ugh. Can you paste the most recent audit snippet you have?
maya: Sure, here is the create event we do see: ```k8s-audit: {"verb":"create","user":"system:serviceaccount:priv-ops:keystore-proxy","objectRef":{"resource":"secrets","name":"redwood-keystore"}}``` then nothing logged for the subsequent decrypt call.
jordan: That pattern usually means the GET is audited but the downstream KMS decrypt (proxied) isn't hitting the audit policy or is blocked before the audit forwarder. Could be svcacct token-exchange or egress drop. @olivia any RBAC changes in yesterday's deploy?
olivia: I rolled a tightened serviceaccount policy yesterday limiting secrets:get to the priv-ops namespace. I didn't touch the keystore-proxy role, but I did change a rolebinding.
maya: Also noticed a netpol denies egress to our metadata/KMS-forwarder IP range for a subset of pods. That could be preventing the audit-forwarder from shipping logs.
ben: Quick triage checklist: 1) confirm keystore-proxy logs (debug) 2) check k8s audit policy for requestObject/responseObject for decrypt endpoints 3) verify netpol egress for the keystore pod 4) check keystore proxy health /metrics and forwarder status (queue length) 5) validate KMS client lib version on the proxy.
maya: Running checks now. Marking P1 for visibility until we scope.
sec_ops_bot: Incident INC-2024-1187 created and assigned to eng-security team — https://incident.internal/INC-2024-1187.
dinesh: If audit forwarding is flaky, temp mitigation: enable host-level syslog forwarding from the node where keystore pod runs (bypass pod-level forwarder) so decrypts are captured. Also consider adding a dedicated TCP allow in netpol to the forwarder IP.
olivia: Also run: ```kubectl auth can-i get secrets --as=system:serviceaccount:priv-ops:keystore-proxy -n priv-ops``` to confirm effective perms.
maya: Ran that — output: "yes". So SA can get secrets, but decrypt still missing. Next step: tcpdump egress from keystore-proxy pod to confirm packets reach forwarder/KMS.
jordan: Check KMS client too — older client versions sometimes don't propagate request metadata that the forwarder relies on. See runbook page 3.
maya: Update: tcpdump showed egress to forwarder blocked by netpol for IPv4 range 10.240.5.0/24. I temporarily added an explicit egress allow to forwarder and started seeing decrypt audit entries.
ben: Nice. That points to netpol as root cause for the missing audit events.
olivia: Good catch. Long-term fix: tighten netpol by explicit allow for forwarder + host-based forwarder on node as fallback and update runbook to include RBAC/Netpol cross-checks when rolling svcacc changes.
maya: I'll open a PR with: a) netpol patch to add allow to forwarder IPs, b) runbook edit for the keystore audit-forwarder checklist, c) note to validate k8s audit policy after RBAC changes. Linking PR here when ready.
dinesh: Also recommend adding an alert: keystore-forwarder-queue-length > 0 && audit-events-per-minute drops >30% -> page oncall.
oncall: (no response)
maya: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/merge_requests/8422 — includes netpol + runbook + temporary host-forwarder manifest. Needs review from eng-sre and eng-security.
ben: Reviewing now. If we need a hotfix to get immediate telemetry on all nodes I can push the host-forwarder as a one-off daemonset.
maya: Thx — pushing the daemonset as a short-term mitigation while we get the netpol change through.
ojordan: After merge, let's add a postmortem-lite doc with timeline and a checklist for future RBAC rollouts.
maya: Agreed. I'll capture timeline in the runbook PR description and close this thread once PR merges. :thumbsup:
